file.content:
datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

generator client {
  provider        = "prisma-client-js"
  previewFeatures = []
}

model Article {
  id          Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  slug        String    @unique
  title       String
  description String
  body        String
  createdAt   DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime  @default(now())
  tagList     Tag[]
  author      User      @relation("UserArticles", fields: [authorId], onDelete: Cascade, references: [id])
  authorId    Int
  favoritedBy User[]    @relation("UserFavorites")
  comments    Comment[]
}

model Comment {
  id        Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @default(now())
  body      String
  article   Article  @relation(fields: [articleId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  articleId Int
  author    User     @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  authorId  Int
}

model Tag {
  id       Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  name     String    @unique
  articles Article[]
}

model User {
  id         Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  email      String    @unique
  username   String    @unique
  password   String
  image      String?   @default("https://api.realworld.io/images/smiley-cyrus.jpeg")
  bio        String?
  articles   Article[] @relation("UserArticles")
  favorites  Article[] @relation("UserFavorites")
  followedBy User[]    @relation("UserFollows")
  following  User[]    @relation("UserFollows")
  comments   Comment[]
  demo       Boolean   @default(false)
}

**Answers to the six questions**

1. **Who may edit (R1):** The repository has no written rule. `deleteComment` and `updateArticle` in `app/src/app/routes/article/article.service.ts` both allow only the author. This is inferred from code.
2. **Edit time limit (R2):** Not in the repository. The only "expiresIn" is the JWT lifetime in `auth/token.utils.ts`, which is a login token, not an edit window. I assumed there is no limit.
3. **Edited mark (R3):** `Comment` already has `updatedAt` in `schema.prisma`. The existing code sets it by hand on edits (`updateArticle` does). The spec uses it as the mark, so no new column and no migration are needed. The repository has no rule on what a migration that adds a mark must do, so I do not know that answer.
4. **Error shape and codes (R4):** `HttpException` in `app/src/app/models/http-exception.model.ts`, handled in `app/src/main.ts`. The handler sends the exception's message as the JSON body. The 401 handler uses a different shape, `{status, message}`.
5. **Migrations (R7):** `app/README.md` says to run `npx prisma migrate deploy`. Migrations live in `app/src/prisma/migrations/<timestamp>_<name>/migration.sql`.
6. **Unit tests (R8):** `app/jest.config.ts` matches `src/**/*.test.ts` and `src/**/*.spec.ts`. The existing tests are in `app/src/tests/services/`. Run them with `npm test`, which calls `nx test`.

**Conflict: non-author edit.** Two sources disagree.
- `deleteComment` looks the comment up filtered by author, so a non-author gets **404 (not found)**. Its 403 branch is unreachable.
- `updateArticle` checks the author after lookup, so a non-author gets **403 (forbidden)**.

I followed `deleteComment`, because it is the sibling on the same resource and route shape. If you want 403 instead, that is a one-line change in the spec.

**Other assumptions, not from the repository**
- The comment must belong to the article named in `:slug`, otherwise it is not found.
- The spec does not copy any rule values. The Builder reads them from the named sources.

**Not available:** The README points to `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` at the repository root. That file is not in this working directory, so I could not check it.
